Regular expressions for sample identifiers

regex_ids.Rd

regex_ids is a centralised place for regular expressions (regex) for extracting different identifiers. These expressions are then used by the extract_* series of functions for extracting identifiers.

Regular expressions are written as raw strings using stringr::regex which makes them easier to understand and maintain. The "Regular Expressions" chapter in "R for Data Science" is a great resource for understanding regular expressions.

Usage

regex_ids()

Value

A named list of regular expressions for different identifiers

Details

worksheet: the worksheet identifier is "WS" followed by six numbers, which increase sequentially (i.e "WS000001", "WS000002", WS000003"). Worksheets are the way in which genetic tests are organised into batches within the lab. Worksheet identifiers are generated by DNA Database.

labno: the numeric identifier given to every DNA sample from DNA Database. The regex specifies 8 digits in the identifier, although for samples from 2012 or earlier there will only be 6 digits. This identifier is referred to as "labno" throughout idtools because this is the name used in the "Samples" table of DNA Database.

The first two digits of the labno format are the year the sample was recieved, and then the digits increase with each new sample. For example, the first sample recieved in 2026 would have the labno 26000001.

suffix: if the same DNA sample is tested multiple times on the same worksheet (which can happen for repeatability experiments during test validation) then a suffix letter (usually a-d) is added directly after the labno. Extracting this suffix is useful when assessing the variability between different replicates of the same sample.

igene_rno: the R (referral) number from the iGene database has the format of R followed by the two-digit year number, a hyphen, and then four alpha-numeric charactes. Example: R26-AB12.

Examples


file_string <- "WS123456_12345678_sequencing_results.xlsx"

stringr::str_extract(file_string,
                      pattern = regex_ids()$labno_suffix$regex,
                      group = regex_ids()$labno_suffix$labno_group)
#> [1] "12345678"
